newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnia's central bank gets French governor.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia's central bank gets French governor.

text.p: Bosnia's three-man presidency on Tuesday endorsed a Frenchman appointed by the International Monetary Fund as governor of its central bank, an international mediator said.

Carl Bildt, the international official charged with overseeing civilian implementation of Bosnia's peace accord, said the presidency also appointed three Bosnian members of the bank's governing board for a six-year term.
The bank is yet to begin its work which will include setting of monetary policy and issuing of currency throughout Bosnia- Hercegovina in line with a post-war constitution.
The new governor, Serge Robert, will be able to cast tie-breaking votes in the bank board's decision-making.
Meeting for the fourth time, the three national leaders, a Serb, Croat and Moslem, also discussed foreign affairs and ministerial appointments, Bildt said.

The three national leaders also agreed to step up the pace of their meetings while working on setting up joint institutions and agreed to meet twice a week, alternately in Serb and Moslem-Croat territory.
